notes: In some etyma *t before *o was palatalised as before *i and *e (Table 8); in others it kept the reflex it has before *a and *u (Table 7). All SV languages agree etymon by etymon (p. 268), and Lynch takes this as evidence that POc '*o' was in part a front or central vowel, POc *ə (§7).
A subregularity: *u > i after *ol, in Ura, the Tanna languages and Anejom̃; the final *i is needed to condition the reflex of the preceding *l (Table 5).
examples: *tolu > ANJ e/sej, URA ge/hli; *ma-tolu > ANJ a/mesej

notes: In part of the vocabulary *l before *o has the reflex it has before *a and *u, not the palatalised j (Table 4a); the row of Lynch (2001: 44) gives j before *o.
In the three northern Tanna languages PTN *l (from POc *l, *r and retained *R) became i, often phonetically [j], before *a and *u (11); before *i, and probably *e, it remained l (12).
